source: Asmarino Independent Media: 'URGENT Eritrea: A serious Case of Cholera Outbreak' (10 September 2016)

source: Martin Plaut, 'Eritrea: drought, hunger and malnutrition - the evidence' (27 October 2016)
processing_notes: Source states: 'People have been forced to draw water from pits dug into the Mereb river. It is the main source of a cholera outbreak in the area. So far 1342 patients have been registered and 13 deaths have been reported in one makeshift clinic alone. The numbers are worst in Upper Gash where the outbreak was first reported' - cholera confirmed present; no case count available.

source: Assenna.com: 'Reliable sources from Eritrea indicate a cholera epidemic which has started in the Dembelas and Quahayn areas is rapidly spreading to Gash-Barka region' (30 September 2016)
processing_notes: Source states: 'The epidemic seems to have started in the Dembelas and Qwohayn areas and is sweeping through the Gash Barka region; All movements into and from the area have been barred, Aqurdet being the outpost of the limited zone, coming from Keren; The weekly market days have been halted' - cholera confirmed present; no case count available.

source: Radio Erena (Tigrinya), 'While cholera is attacking people in Zoba Gash-Barka, the Ministry of Health gives Barentu residents training on preventing communicable diseases' (article 2585, archived 30 September 2016)
processing_notes: Source states: 'While cholera is reported to be attacking people in several areas of Zoba Gash-Barka, the Ministry of Health, Gash-Barka branch, gave training to the people of Barentu on the prevention of communicable diseases; In the areas of Zoba Gash-Barka bordering Ethiopia and Sudan, sources from the country indicate cholera is attacking people, although the Government of Eritrea has so far given no information or warning about this [translated from Tigrinya]' - cholera confirmed present; no case count available.

source: Radio Erena (Tigrinya), quoting a WHO spokesperson via RFI: 'In Eritrea, we have no official report of cholera appearing' (article 2595, 4 October 2016; WHO statement dated 29 September 2016)
processing_notes: Source states: 'While it is reported that cholera is attacking people in Eritrea, the World Health Organization has said it has no official information so far. A WHO spokesperson, in information sent to Radio France Internationale, was able to confirm that the disease has appeared on the borders of Ethiopia close to Eritrea. The organization also mentions that the Eritrean Ministry of Health is making preparations so that the disease does not spread into Eritrea [translated from Tigrinya]' - cholera confirmed present; no case count available.

source: Radio Erena (Tigrinya), 'Because of the threat of cholera, the disrupted legal movement at the Eritrea-Sudan border has returned to normal' (article 2623, 11 December 2016)
processing_notes: Source states: 'The free movement of people to and from Eritrea-Sudan, which had been cut off for the past months, returned to normal from last week; Erena's sources recalled that this does not mean the threat of cholera around the Eritrea-Sudan border has been entirely removed [translated from Tigrinya]' - cholera confirmed present; no case count available.
